This multiple spawning strategy enables the species to spread reproductive effort across the favorable environmental windows typical of tropical reef ecosystems.

Captive-rearing studies and long-term field observations have provided insight into the lifespan of Yellowband parrotfish under natural thermal conditions. The maximum recorded longevity for Scarus schlegeli at 27.6 °C is approximately 15 years [am = approximately 15 years], a value that positions this species among the shorter-lived member at a temperature of 27.6 °C [T = 27.6 °C]s of the genus. The ultimate total length of 40 cm [Li = 40 cm] places this species in the small to medium size range among parrotfishes, considerably smaller than the massive humphead parrotfish Bolbometopon muricatum but larger than diminutive species like Scarus psittacus. Ecological interactions with other herbivorous fishes on the reef are influenced by these size parameters, as larger individuals can access more heavily defended algal turfs and can compete more effectively for high-quality foraging territories.
